_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership (Jun-2026), moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for the Ramkrishna Forgings initiation. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

indiaCv.fy27OutlookPct: 4-6% (ICRA, as quoted in the FY26 annual report)

usTrucks.comment: A 'bottoming' year: weak freight demand, high costs, tariff uncertainty; strong close to the year (AR FY26)

industry.tariffs: US tariffs on Indian goods and Section 232 duties on truck parts hit FY26 exports (standalone exports -20%, North America -35%); management said in May-2026 that 'the tariff is behind us' and contracts pass currency and steel through with a quarter's lag.
industry.costs: Energy (gas, power) and shipping are the main unrecovered costs: shipping +15-20% and transit +15-20 days after the West Asia conflict (Q4FY26 call, May-2026).

excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: exceptional charges in three of the last four quarters (Rs358 cr in Jun-2026, which turned the quarter into a loss), so its ~93x trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on depressed EPS (same exclusion as the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda, Sona, Craftsman, Belrise and JBM initiations).
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring), so there is no five-year median (same exclusion as the other auto-component initiations).

peers.self: RKFORGE itself is left out of the de-rating (its own trailing P/E of ~113x sits on trough FY26 earnings).
peers.note: The auto-component peer set used by the Bosch, Motherson, Uno Minda, Sona, Craftsman, Belrise and JBM Auto initiations (their union), Ramkrishna Forgings itself left out. SCHAEFFLER (December year-end) has P/E history from Feb-2023, ZFCVINDIA from May-2022 and MSUMI from Apr-2022: their medians cover the history available. Forging peers (Bharat Forge, Happy Forgings, GNA Axles, CIE Automotive, Craftsman) are shown in the peer table for reference; Happy Forgings (listed Dec-2023) has no five-year median and CIE reports on December years. Peer multiples at the 30-Sep-2026 close from tools/authoring/asof-peers.js.

street._note: Coverage is thin and mostly behind logins. Notes standing on 30-Sep-2026 that we could read: Dalal & Broacha (1-Jun-2026). The S&P Global consensus (via StockAnalysis, 31-Jul-2026) shows four analysts, three Hold and one Sell, average target Rs634 (range Rs550-680); individual names were not shown. Monarch Networth (13-Oct-2026, Buy, Rs806, 27x Sep-28E EPS) and Antique (2-Nov-2026, Buy, Rs872, 13x EV/EBITDA) initiated after our as-of date and are not used.

brokers.thesis: Management-meet note: diversification beyond CVs (PV/EV, railways, aluminium forgings), utilisation-led operating leverage, ~200bp margin gain to ~17% by FY28E; 27x for better earnings visibility. Risks: tariffs, leverage.

consensus.note: S&P Global consensus as shown by StockAnalysis; the 31-Jul-2026 average and range come from a dated search extract; the monthly rating split (Jul-Aug 2026: 3 Hold, 1 Sell) and the FY27E/FY28E EPS are from the page's history table (FY28E EPS shown as 'next year' on a later visit, so treat it as indicative).

moat: Scale and range
Second-largest Indian forger; 3.96 lakh t capacity across hammer, press, ring rolling, cold/warm forging, castings and machining
AMBER
Breadth helps win full-axle and engine programmes, but Bharat Forge is several times larger and smaller rivals (Happy Forgings, GNA) earn higher margins
Customer relationships

Long-standing supplier to Indian and North American/European truck makers (customers not named in our sources); programme lives of ~4 years; 109-363 new products developed a year by facility (AR FY26)
GREEN
Qualified positions on safety-critical parts are sticky; switching costs are real
Pricing power
Steel passed through with a quarter's lag; energy, freight not passed through; FY25-26 margins fell to 14-15%
RED
A price-taker with powerful OEM customers
Cost position
Jamshedpur cluster near steel suppliers; integrated machining
AMBER
FY22-24 margins of 21-22% show what full plants earn; utilisation is the swing factor
Diversification
Railways 7.5%, mining/farm 5.9%, PV/EV and aluminium early; wheel JV with an assured Indian Railways offtake
AMBER
Still ~75% CV-linked; the wheel JV is the one genuinely protected new business
critiques: Accounting and controls: a Rs220.5 cr inventory overstatement (FY25, Rs50 cr in FY24) found only at the year-end count; ratings moved to Negative/downgraded; it will take clean years to rebuild trust.
Repeated over-promising: the Rs8,000 cr revenue target has moved from FY28 to FY29; FY26 revenue grew 5%.
Capital intensity: Rs2,958 cr of investing cash flow in FY24-26 against Rs1,494 cr of operating cash flow; net debt ~Rs1,900 cr; ROCE 5.6% in FY26.
Reported EPS is noisy: FY25 EPS of Rs22.9 included a Rs193 cr deferred-tax credit and an Rs83 cr gain from a sold subsidiary; on clean earnings FY25 EPS was ~Rs6.
Promoter pledge: 15.6% of promoter shares (6.75% of the company) pledged at Jun-2026.
gaps: Broker notes standing on 30-Sep-2026: only Dalal & Broacha (1-Jun-2026) could be read; the S&P consensus (4 analysts) does not show names. Monarch and Antique initiated after 30-Sep-2026 and are not used.

The 24-Sep-2026 NSE allotment filing did not load for us; the conversion (34 lakh shares, Rs149.94 cr, 18,55,70,017 shares) is taken from search extracts of that filing and the warrant terms in the FY26 annual report.
Standalone domestic/export revenue before FY24: only the revenue-mix percentages (FY22-FY26) are disclosed in our sources.
Forging volumes and realisation by quarter: the presentation charts did not extract cleanly; not used.
Wheel JV economics (capex, debt, pricing) are not disclosed; our JV share of profit is an estimate from the 40,000/80,000-wheel offtake and the Rs400-450 cr revenue indication.
Exact date of the Globe All India Services sale (FY25) not in our sources.
Original (pre-restatement) FY24 accounts: Screener and the company now show FY24 restated for the Rs50.22 cr inventory overstatement; we use the restated figures.
conflicts: Inventory discrepancy: first estimated at 4-5% of net worth (Apr-2025), finally Rs220.52 cr at Mar-25 and Rs50.22 cr at Mar-24 (~6.7% of net worth); one press report cites ~Rs270 cr (both years added).

FY25 deferred tax credit: the call transcript quoted ~Rs223 cr; the annual report shows a Rs187.4 cr asset on ACIL's losses plus other items (FY25 consolidated deferred tax credit Rs193.0 cr). We use the annual report.
Capex guidance FY27: Rs300-400 cr incl. Rs50 cr JV (May-2026) vs ~Rs350 cr (Jul-2026). We use Rs350 cr.
